object_description: low-rise complex of six parallel pavilion rows
design_condition: Set back in the existing orchard, the low-rise complex follows a horizontal base across the slope, recreates the walled garden and uses interior courtyards to connect the buildings with the park and surrounding landscape.

positive.statement: The low pavilion form integrates harmoniously into the rural village, castle and park.
The irregular exterior outline blends into the landscape while the regular solids-and-voids pattern supports variety and orientation.
The ground-floor interior street structures the different functions favorably and provides landmarks and natural light.
The accommodation units offer high-quality strolling spaces and a variety of living spaces.
The restored vegetable garden and diversified outdoor program support daily contact and exchanges between inhabitants and residents.
The low elevation allows the castle roofs to emerge and avoids competition with the historic complex.

negative.statement: The first-floor interior street tends to separate the functions rather than structure them.
The upper accommodation level is divided into two distant centers and is too compressed in places.
The bathrooms and their access are poorly designed.
The constructive principles should be specified at the level of the supporting structure and facade.
The multiplied gable roofs almost produce the opposite of the intended village integration.
The project lacks a clear entry gesture and the street-side clearance needed for proper functioning.
The building has a large influence on the plot, a significant built volume and an introverted attitude toward public space.
The management of the topography at the car park and underground access is poorly regulated.
The spread of the project and extensive horizontal circulation increase the accommodation area beyond target.
The multiplicity of roofs places the project toward the higher end of the cost range.
The underground car park has a significant impact on the total cost.
